change: the analysis player finds a signed-in student: the 1.1 lab page named a localStorage key nothing writes, so no teacher lock could bind anyone
_context: Reported as "it didn't lock when the teacher locked it for a student", hours after
board 277 opened the anonymous case.
NOT A REGRESSION FROM 277, and worth being exact about that. The page has always
read localStorage 'apcs_student_token'. Nothing writes it: shopify/join.html line
563 sets 'apcse_token' at sign-in, theme.liquid decides 'logged-in-student' by
reading it, and all 20 token references in the theme use it. So a signed-in
student has always sent no Authorization header on that page.
It was invisible because the anonymous rule in force until 277 refused anonymous
callers anyway, so the page LOOKED locked and the missing token changed nothing
observable. Opening the anonymous case is what made a missing token start to
matter. The live page proves it on its own bytes: 'apcse_token' appears at offset
96777, put there by the theme's own tracker, and the analysis mount at 229910
reads a different key.
FIXED IN THE PLAYER, NOT THE PAGE, and that is the whole design of it. The player
is served from this API with no-store and costs a push; a page body costs a live
Matrixify MERGE with no undo. So an EMPTY answer from the page's configured
getToken now falls through to the resolution the lab player has always had. The
live page needs no import.
The same defect was found in public/heartbeat-reporter.js by grepping the other
consumers rather than by waiting for a second report.
